record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of simple polygons.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 32 Characterize visibility graphs of simple polygons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A simple polygon P in the Euclidean plane is a closed, non-self-intersecting polygonal curve together with its bounded interior. Two vertices u and v of P are said to be visible to each other if the closed straight-line segment uv is contained in the closure of P (i.e., the segment lies inside P or along its boundary, with no part exiting through the exterior). The (vertex) visibility graph of P is the simple graph whose vertex set is the set of vertices of P, and in which two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if they are visible to each other (in particular, every pair of consecutive polygon vertices is adjacent, so the graph contains the boundary cycle of P as a Hamiltonian cycle).

Give a combinatorial characterization of the class of visibility graphs of simple polygons. Equivalently, determine a list of necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions on a graph G (possibly with a distinguished Hamiltonian cycle) so that G is isomorphic to the visibility graph of some simple polygon.
artifact.status_search_result: The combinatorial characterization of visibility graphs of simple polygons is widely regarded as a long-standing open problem in computational/combinatorial geometry. Only partial results are known: a few necessary conditions, characterizations for restricted polygon classes (e.g., spiral and tower polygons), and a complete characterization for the related class of pseudo-polygon visibility graphs. The recognition problem is not even known to lie in NP. No general characterization has been published as of 2026.

status_evidence.snippet: An efficient algorithmic characterization of the visibility graphs of simple polygons is unknown. The problem is not even known to be in NP.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of visibility graphs of simple polygons remains unknown.

status_evidence.snippet: Characterization given for pseudo-polygons, leaving the simple-polygon case open.
status_evidence.claim: Only the pseudo-polygon variant has a known characterization.
